post.caption: Only one gem can be called cat's-eye. In the trade, plain cat's-eye means the gem chrysoberyl, and other stones need a prefix, like quartz cat's-eye. A band of light reflects from thin, parallel inclusions inside the stone, and the stone is cut as a cabochon so the band shows. The cutter lines the base up with those inclusions. Jewelers call the light and dark halves milk and honey. Its colors run from honey brown to greenish yellow, and it measures 8.5 on the Mohs scale. Sri Lanka and Brazil are two main sources. Alexandrite is a color-change variety of the same mineral.
